terms.comment: Set apart, and so private or secret (Lewis & Short). As a noun, sēcrētum is a secret or a private talk: sēcrētum petit, he asks for a word in private (Plin. Ep. 1.5.11, Lewis & Short).
Lewis & Short: in secret, without witnesses, in private. Traupman: velim tēcum loquī sēcrētō, I want to speak with you privately.
Against in pūblicō, in public (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem, lībertō tuō, dīxerīs.
phrases.english: This is between ourselves: keep it to yourself, and don’t tell even your freedman Apella.

phrases.latin: Mālim tēcum dē eā in prīvātō loquī.
phrases.english: I’d rather talk to you about that in private.
